title: Rectangle with Initializer List
prompt_md:
## Goal
Give `Rectangle` a constructor that sets its width and height. Because both members are `const`, you have to set them with a member initializer list (lesson 14.10) — assignment inside the constructor body will not compile.

## Input
One line: two integers `W` and `H` separated by a space (1 ≤ W, H ≤ 1000).

## Output
One line: `Area: X`, where `X` is `W * H`.

## Task
Write the constructor `Rectangle(int width, int height)` so it initializes the two `const` members from its parameters. The `area()` accessor and the driver in `main` are already provided.

title: Incrementer with a Reference Member
prompt_md:
## Goal
A reference data member lets a class operate directly on a variable that lives outside the class. Build an `Incrementer` that repeatedly adds a fixed amount to an external integer.

## Input
One line: three integers `initial`, `amount`, and `count`.

## Output
One line: `Total: X`, where `X` is `initial + amount * count`.

## Task
`Incrementer` has a reference member `m_target` (bound to an external `int`) and a `const int` member `m_amount`. Write its constructor using a member initializer list (lesson 14.10): a reference member and a `const` member can only be initialized there, never assigned in the body. The provided `apply()` adds `m_amount` to the referenced variable; `main` constructs an `Incrementer` over a local `total` and calls `apply()` `count` times.
